svg.title: Comparing relative position in two normal distributions
svg.desc: Two normal curves on the same axis. The wider one has mean 60 and standard deviation 10; the narrower, taller one has mean 75 and standard deviation 5. A mark at 70 on the first and a mark at 80 on the second each sit exactly one standard deviation above their own distribution's mean. The raw values differ by 10, and the distributions differ in both centre and spread, yet the two marks describe the same relative position: each has about 84 per cent of its own distribution below it. That is what a z-score measures, and it is why a percentile can be compared between two different normal distributions while a raw value cannot. Illustrative data.
svg.text: Different mean and spread, but one z-score fixes the same relative position
70 here and 80 there are both z = 1, so both are at about the 84th percentile.
